title: Jason: Aeetes and the Tasks
subtitle: Fire-breathing bulls, dragon teeth, and a king who intends betrayal

main.author: Apollonius Rhodius
main.locator: Argonautica 3, Aeetes sets the trial; Book 3, normalized characters 22216-22948
main.excerpt: Two bulls with feet of bronze I have that pasture on the plain of Ares, breathing forth flame from their jaws; them do I yoke and drive over the stubborn field of Ares, four plough-gates; and quickly cleaving it with the share up to the headland, I cast into the furrows the seed, not the corn of Demeter, but the teeth of a dread serpent that grow up into the fashion of armed men; them I slay at once, cutting them down beneath my spear as they rise against me on all sides. In the morning do I yoke the oxen, and at eventide I cease from the harvesting. And thou, if thou wilt accomplish such deeds as these, on that very day shalt carry off the fleece to the king’s palace; ere that time comes I will not give it, expect it not.

aid.excerpt: And at dawn steep this charm in water, strip, and anoint thy body therewith as with oil; and in it there will be boundless prowess and mighty strength, and thou wilt deem thyself a match not for men but for the immortal gods. And besides, let thy spear and shield and sword be sprinkled. Thereupon the spear-heads of the earthborn men shall not pierce thee, nor the flame of the deadly bulls as it rushes forth resistless.

narrativeBlocks.title: Colchis at the world's edge
narrativeBlocks.body: The Argo survives clashing rocks, hostile kingdoms, and the loss of Heracles along the way — and reaches Colchis, at the edge of the known world, where the fleece hangs in a grove guarded by a sleepless dragon.

narrativeBlocks.title: King Aeetes's price
narrativeBlocks.body: Aeetes, the fearsome local king, will not simply give his treasure to foreigners. His price: yoke his pair of fire-breathing bronze-hooved bulls, plough a field with them, and sow the teeth of a dragon.

narrativeBlocks.title: An impossible morning
narrativeBlocks.body: Each task alone kills ordinary men: the bulls burn you, and the sown teeth spring up as armed warriors who kill the sower. Aeetes has no intention of honouring the bargain either — succeed, and he plans to destroy the Greeks anyway.

narrativeBlocks.title: The watching princess
narrativeBlocks.body: In the palace, Aeetes's daughter Medea — a priestess and sorceress — watches the stranger undertake her father's murderous test. The gods arrange that she falls in love, and everything hinges on which loyalty she chooses.

narrativeBlocks.title: Tasks as a mythic pattern
narrativeBlocks.body: Impossible tasks set by a hostile king recur everywhere (Heracles' labours, Bellerophon's missions). The pattern tests two things at once: can the hero do them — and does the king keep his word? Usually one fails.

quiz.prompt: What tasks does Aeetes set Jason for the fleece?

choices.text: Yoke his fire-breathing bulls, plough a field, and sow dragon's teeth that sprout armed warriors
Retrieve a golden apple from the Hesperides

quiz.explanation: The bulls and dragon-teeth are designed to kill — and Aeetes plans betrayal even if Jason succeeds.

quiz.prompt: Why is Jason still in danger after succeeding?

choices.text: The dragon wakes and cannot be killed
Aeetes never meant to keep his word — he plans to destroy the Greeks regardless of the outcome
The tasks void the bargain by their terms
His own crew mutinies in Colchis

quiz.explanation: The tasks are a trap within a trap; only inside help can get Jason out alive.
